ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, Special Economic Measures Act schedules, Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List where a US nexus exists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and applicable provincial securities administrative enforcement lists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are assessed in accordance with FATF 40 Recommendations and FINTRAC guidance; enhanced customer due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions and non-resident shareholders. All screening results must be evidenced, risk-rated and retained in the corporate onboarding file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Access (NUANS Name Search, Name Reservation and Incorporation Filing Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Alberta must be in English or French using the standard Roman alphabet, Arabic numerals and limited punctuation; non-Roman scripts such as Chinese characters, Cyrillic or ideographic scripts are not accepted in a corporate name. Foreign words must be transliterated into Roman characters and may require an accompanying English or French translation in the name search report. The name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive or optional element, and a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd. or Limited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed corporate name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, accompanied by a fresh NUANS Name Search Report and a written explanation establishing that there is no reasonable likelihood of confusion with any existing name. If the Director acting under the Alberta Business Corporations Act maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Alberta Court of King's Bench for judicial review through an originating application. There is no statutory extension of the 90-day Name Search Report validity; if the 90-day window lapses before incorporation, a new NUANS report must be procured.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in principle for this low-risk plush toy OEM industry, provided the virtual office provider maintains a real physical Alberta address where notices and legal process can be served, operates during business hours, and does not rely on a post office box or mail-forwarding-only address. The Alberta Business Corporations Act requires a registered office in Alberta, but does not require the registered office to be the location of business operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified as LOW (5–10%) for a standard-risk plush toy OEM. Unannounced physical on-site inspections are not routine for incorporation, but may occur through municipal licensing enforcement, financial institution KYC/site visits during bank account opening, or targeted FINTRAC compliance reviews. The registered office cannot avoid service of process and physical access obligations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; key sections: 5 (incorporation), 10 (articles), 23 (registered office), 82 (directors), 91 (officers), 101 (share subscriptions), 134 (initial resolution).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) together with Initial Notice of Directors (Form 2) and Notice of Registered Office (Form 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required; the incorporator may authorize and issue at least one common share without nominal or par value. No escrow account is required for a non-licensed commercial corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporator subscribe for 100 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share, accept the articles, and direct the corporate secretary to issue share certificates upon receipt of funds. The registered office located at Suite 200, 88 Eau Claire Way SW, Calgary, Alberta, approved. John Schmidt is appointed sole director and President; Marie Lacroix is appointed Secretary; the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, engage counsel, and adopt financial signing authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Online (NUANS search through Service Alberta authorized providers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS Name Search Request for the proposed corporate name, review the distinctiveness report, and reserve the name for 90 days through the online corporate registry system.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for distinctiveness, file a new NUANS search with a revised name or obtain written consent from the existing entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 Articles of Incorporation, Form 2 Initial Notice of Directors, and Form 3 Notice of Registered Office. All incorporators must sign and date the forms; ensure the registered office is an actual physical address in Alberta.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry staff may reject incomplete forms; correct any errors and refile within 30 days of query notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Online (corporate and business service portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed forms to the online registry and remit the incorporation fee and applicable search fee using a credit card or pre-authorized debit; print the payment receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If system validation fails, amend the affected form and resubmit; if an additional declaration is requested, provide a sworn affidavit within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registry approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and certified Articles; verify the legal name, registered office, and director information; keep the certificate in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued due to incomplete filing, correct the record and pay any late filing penalty before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and Corporate Secretary under Alberta Business Corporations Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt By-Law No. 1, appoint officers, open a corporate bank account using the Certificate and registered office confirmation, issue share certificates, and file the initial Alberta annual return and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) corporate tax account registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA business number is not issued promptly, contact the CRA business desk; maintain a complete corporate record book and resubmit any rejected tax registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration Exemption under Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) Schedule A – low-impact textile/sewing operation; no full EIA mandated
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal wastewater discharge limits: BOD < 300 mg/L, COD < 600 mg/L, TSS < 300 mg/L; no VOCs requiring capture where water-based adhesives are used; non-hazardous textile offcuts must be reused, recycled, or disposed at an approved municipal facility

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification per Alberta Fire Code (occupancy and egress); building occupancy/structural load inspection for commercial floor use; Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) clearance and Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) site compliance for sewing and ultrasonic welding equipment

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first complete any required federal or provincial corporate registration (e.g., extra-provincial registration in Alberta or federal incorporation via Corporations Canada), then apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or through the Business Registration Online service. The BN serves as the statutory TIN; separate GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax program accounts are established during the same e-registration process. Non-resident applicants without a Canadian presence may use the CRA's non-resident registration channel and may be required to designate a representative or provide an address in Canada for service of documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; a business corporation incorporated in Canada is automatically subject to entity-level corporate income tax under Part I of the Income Tax Act, whether organized federally or under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Relevant elections and anti-hybrid rules include the section 18.4, 18.5, and 18.6 hybrid mismatch elections (OECD BEPS Action 2), the subsection 256(2) deemed acquisition-of-control election, the section 216(1) non-resident rental election, and the CCPC status elections available on CRA prescribed forms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax; no Alberta provincial sales tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold (measured on taxable supplies made worldwide in any single calendar quarter and in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters); a non-resident supplier carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada may be required to register regardless of the threshold under section 240 of the Excise Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a federal or Alberta real-time e-invoicing clearance mandate, API requirement, or digital stamping regime. GST/HST registrants may issue paper, PDF, or EDI invoices. Electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million, and all registrants may file via CRA NETFILE or API-enabled digital services. No pre-clearance of invoices is required by fiscal authorities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may zero-rate exports of tangible personal property where the goods are supplied in Canada and delivered by the supplier to a common carrier, customs broker, or the recipient for export, and the goods are exported from Canada as part of that supply. The registrant must retain documentary evidence of export within the prescribed period (generally 60 days for the zero-rating to be claimed on that return). Services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated when performed wholly outside Canada, or when supplied directly in furtherance of a non-resident's commercial activity, subject to the exclusions in Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) accepted and processed by the CBSA
Bill of Lading issued by the common carrier or freight forwarder evidencing shipment from Canada to the foreign customer
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Settlement Statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds in CAD
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess to recover uncollected GST/HST plus interest and applicable penalties on a retrospective basis if export documentation is inadequate or the supply is found not to be zero-rated. Penalties under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act for false statements or omissions generally equal the greater of CAD 250 and 50% of the net tax assessed; section 285 carries additional penalties for wilful evasion or fraud, and criminal prosecution may follow. In cases of fraudulent export zero-rating, the CRA may also invoke joint liability of the exporter and purchaser, impose a 6-year reassessment period for misrepresentation, and issue fines for failure to retain records for six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential banking regulation is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing supervision is exercised by FINTRAC. Canada does not operate a dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority. The Minister of Finance has broad residual powers under the Currency Act and the Bank Act, but current policy imposes no centralized exchange-control license.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains free convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Canadian dollar has a floating exchange-rate regime and there is no general restriction on conversion, no registration of FX contracts, and no central-bank prior approval for inbound investment, dividend declarations, interest payments, royalty payments, loan repayments, or repatriation of equity sale proceeds. For the Alberta business corporation engaged in ISIC 3240 plush-toy OEM, outward profit remittance to a non-resident shareholder is legally unrestricted but subject to Part XIII withholding tax at the statutory 25% or a lower applicable Canada-U.S./Canada-U.K./other treaty rate, requiring a properly executed Form NR301/NR302 waiver evidence package, Form NR4 filings, and CRA payment. Additional constraints include Canada Revenue Agency transfer-pricing documentation under section 247, thin-capitalization limits under section 18(4)-(6), and the requirement that material cross-border commercial transactions satisfy the arm's-length standard. The Investment Canada Act notification thresholds do not apply to a passive export-oriented service entity unless acquiring control of a Canadian business above the monetary threshold; nevertheless, a share-subscription wiring memorandum should be maintained to evidence foreign direct investment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no Canadian statutory surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no timeline for repatriation of export proceeds. A Canadian exporter may retain foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency bank account or in an offshore account, may convert at negotiated commercial rates, and may use those proceeds directly for offshore supplier payments. For corporate tax and GST/HST reporting, all export revenues and purchases must be translated into Canadian dollars using the CRA published annual average exchange rate for cash-basis or accrual-basis entries, or the spot rate on the transaction date where the CRA method permits. No Form T2125 reporting category is required for export proceeds merely because they are earned in USD, but the transaction must be reflected in the accounts with traceable USD CAD conversion records, supplier invoices, and bank statements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational CAD/USD Current Account
Operational Account with integrated cross-border USD treasury
Operational Account and FX Hedging Facility
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Finance/Commercial Letter of Credit Account
Operational Account and Platform-Pay Merchant Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary payment collection, Low as the primary treasury account. Canada does not recognize the European EMI licence. An offshore digital EMI that offers multi-currency IBANs may lawfully service a Canadian corporate client as a money-services business only if it is registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, maintains a Canadian agent or authorized representative, and executes fund flows through a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank or an approved clearing agent. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act, foreign payment service providers that acquire Canadian end-users are expected to register with the Bank of Canada once the retail payments framework is fully in force. For a CA_AB plush-mask mascot manufacturer, a foreign EMI should be used only for low-value platform collections, not for capital contributions, trade settlements over CAD 10,000, or payroll disbursements, because the local bank will not extend commercial credit or trade finance against an EMI balance. All funds held at an EMI remain outside Canadian deposit insurance and are not covered by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no Alberta statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically in front of a bank branch for account opening. Major Canadian banks accept remote onboarding where the corporate applicant is verified through the following process: (1) submission of certified true copies of incorporation documents; (2) digital identity verification of every director and every Person of Significant Control (PSC) using FINTRAC-compliant technology, such as government-issued credential scanning plus live liveness check and third-party data cross-match; (3) notarization or banker's authentication where the client resides outside Canada; (4) a remote video-conference KYC interview with at least one director and the beneficial owner or authorized signing officer. Some Tier 1 banks reserve the right to require an in-person visit for the first account or where the corporate ownership structure involves non-OECD-resident parties. For an Alberta Business Corporation with a registered office in Calgary or Edmonton, remote opening is generally feasible if the company provides a verifiable physical office address, active email domain, and a video meeting conducted by the corporate secretary. The bank may also require production of the Alberta corporate registry extracts, the CBCA/Alberta PSC register, and a notice of assessment for any Canadian resident director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-office formation through a commercial agent with no evidence of an active operational premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation; Alberta corporate registry extract; registered-office address lease or virtual-office service agreement; act of establishment in the form of a board resolution; business email and website; letter from the accountant confirming physical business activities in ISIC 3240; recent utility bill or lease invoice; notarized passport copies of all directors; executed corporate minute book containing organizational resolutions and share issuances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to identify the ultimate natural-person beneficial owner, especially where a U.S., Chinese, or Hong Kong holding entity appears on the share register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBCA or Alberta PSC register naming each individual with significant control; full share register with addresses and dates of birth; share subscription and transfer agreements; trust deed and trustee declaration, if any nominee structure exists; source-of-wealth declaration from the ultimate shareholder; management account of the immediate parent entity; confirmation that no bearer shares exist and that all transfers have Alberta Form 7 filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital remittance from a jurisdiction listed as high-risk or a non-treaty jurisdiction, giving rise to source-of-funds suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed board resolution authorizing the equity injection; share subscription agreement; bank-to-bank MT103 record showing the originating bank and shareholder name; audited or tax-prepared financial statements of the remitting entity; bank reference letter from the source bank; tax residence certificate; proof that the remittance path has no transit through a sanctions-designated institution; investment declaration under the Investment Canada Act if thresholds are exceeded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-document mismatch caused by high-volume OEM production under platform orders, resulting in invoices, bills of lading, and customs declarations that do not align with settlement amounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master purchase agreements with major U.S./EU retail and licensing clients; purchase orders, proforma invoices, commercial invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading; Canada Border Services Agency export declarations; factory inspection certificates or third-party quality reports for plush toys under ASTM F963 / EN71 / CPSIA; marine or freight insurance certificate; supplier disaggregated cost ledgers; reconciliation spreadsheet showing how Platform-Pay settlements correspond to individual orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A director or beneficial owner matching a politically exposed person (PEP) or sanctions list, or adverse media referring to the company name.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete negative-media search results; device- and biometric-verified identification; sanction-screening report from a commercial AML database; explanation of any PEP status together with bank reference from the home-country regulated institution; detailed curriculum vitae and business references; proof of independence from military, government, or state-controlled procurement; letters of clarification signed under penalty of falsification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of PayPal or Stripe platform payment rails in a business that also makes high-value cross-border payments to Chinese toll manufacturers, creating a perceived mix of consumer receipts and trade-account activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-acquirer merchant statements and settlement reports; PCI-DSS compliance certificate; platform buyer, refund, and chargeback summaries; written explanation of the e-commerce sales channel; supplier due-diligence file including business licences, bank account confirmations, and shareholding identity; transaction-level reconciliation worksheet; bank approval of the merchant gateway prior to activation; commitment to route all supplier payments above CAD 10,000 through SWIFT wire rather than platform systems.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant inbound equity-injection protocol is as follows: (1) the parent shareholder executes a board resolution and share subscription agreement in the exact legal name of the Alberta corporation; (2) the bank account at the source bank must be in the same legal name as the shareholder; (3) the remittance wire must be sent using SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary name matching the Alberta corporate registry extract, beneficiary account held at a Canadian Schedule I bank, and the following purpose-code/text unambiguously stated in Field 70 or 72: 'Share capital contribution / foreign direct investment / ISIC 3240 plush-toy OEM operations'; (4) the funds must be wired directly to the designated Capital Escrow Account, never combined with intercompany loan amounts or trade receivables; (5) the bank's KYC file must contain the source-of-funds evidence, a certificate of the corporate secretary confirming issuance of shares, and confirmation that the shareholder is not a resident of an OFAC/EU-embargoed jurisdiction; (6) once the wire clears and the bank's foreign-exchange conversion is booked, the company's accounting system must record capital at the exact CAD book rate, and any premium/discount on conversion recorded in equity or comprehensive income. For values exceeding C$10,000, the bank will submit its mandatory FINTRAC Report; therefore the corporate file should include a copy of the MT103 and a document trace showing the complete chain from parent board minute to share register entry to bank ledger entry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements, the following clearing rails are permitted and recommended: (a) SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier payments, using beneficiary banks acceptable to the Canadian bank and full Incoterms references; (b) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 through SWIFT MT700/MT707, with deferred payment or sight-draft tenors, for large purchases of polyester fiber and embroidery materials; (c) SWIFT MT202/COV for cross-border bank-to-bank cover payments where the Canadian bank's corresponding relationship requires; (d) Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for high-value Canadian-dollar settlements, and EFT/automated clearing for routine payroll and domestic supplier invoices; (e) SWIFT gpi tracking for end-to-end status confirmation; and (f) approved platform settlement (PayPal, Stripe) for low-value direct-to-consumer collections, with daily sweeps to the main CAD account. The major Canadian banks maintain USD correspondent relationships through their U.S. branches; for RMB payments to Chinese contract manufacturers, a USD-denominated MT103 with the final Chinese beneficiary receiving USD through a correspondent bank is often simpler than a direct RMB clearing, unless the Canadian bank has an approved RMB clearing arrangement. Every outbound disbursement must be supported by a purchase order, supplier invoice, and bank KYC on the supplier, and if the supplier is located in a sanctioned or highly restricted jurisdiction, an Export Control application to Global Affairs Canada and CBSA review is required before payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot and forward contracts in USD/CAD and CNH/CAD (offshore renminbi) executed through a Schedule I Canadian bank or an OSFI-regulated securities dealer.

Outright foreign-exchange forwards with tenors of 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, available on a collateralized or ISDA Master Agreement basis, used solely to hedge committed USD sales receivables and finalized supplier purchase orders.
FX swaps and swap extensions to manage temporary mismatches between inbound USD settlement and outbound USD supplier payments.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNH included as an eligible hedge where the underlying supplier invoice is onshore-CNY-denominated and physical delivery is impracticable; executed with an ISDA credit support annex.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to match long-term USD-denominated purchase contracts against the CAD capital structure, permitted where the notional corresponds to confirmed commercial commitments.
Plain-vanilla FX call and put options, including purchased knock-in or collars, limited to a zero-premium collar strategy for raw-material procurement cycles.
FX collars and participating forwards with a notional cap so that potential hedging loss is narrow and an economic hedge remains demonstrable.

Centrally-cleared USD/CAD futures and options on futures on a registered exchange, such as the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, accessible through a Canadian investment dealer, subject to OSFI margin rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing creates a corporate registry default; two consecutive unfiled annual returns permit the Registrar to administratively strike the corporation from the Alberta register; reinstatement requires filing all overdue returns, paying current fees and applying for revival.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Calgary Tax Services Office / Winnipeg T2 Processing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the corporation's taxation year end (e.g., December 31 year end due by June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; interest accrues at prescribed CRA rates; gross negligence penalties and prosecution possible under the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act an auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders unanimously waive appointment for the fiscal year; an offering corporation cannot waive; no revenue/asset dollar threshold is prescribed in Alberta BCA. A private corporation without unanimous waiver must hold a mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/offering corporations or election to use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) by private corporations under the CPA Canada Handbook; corporate income tax filings use CRA statutory income tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta BCA requires an Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register; the corporation must update the ISC register within 15 days after becoming aware of any change, including share transfers crossing the 25% threshold, and annually confirm and update the register during the corporate secretarial review. There is no separate UBO schedule in the Alberta annual return; however, the register must be made available to enforcement authorities and its completeness considered by directors at each annual meeting.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$120–US$300 per year for registered office/agent service in Alberta if separately engaged; commonly bundled with corporate secretarial services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$8,000 for a statutory audit of a small private Alberta corporation; US$1,500–US$3,500 for a review engagement when the audit is unanimously waived.
